title: Sequence-gap detector and backfill protocol for SSE streams
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Several customers have escalated cases where Hosted API streaming responses are truncated or contain duplicated/overlapping fragments after short disconnects. The problem surface spans Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments but is most commonly reported for Hosted customers behind aggressive load balancers. Root cause appears to be a combination of (1) transient network disconnects causing client reconnects with a last_event_id that doesn't map to the server's in-memory KV/cache boundaries and (2) lack of a server-side small-window replay/backfill protocol, leading to either partial output (clients see missing tokens) or duplicated tokens when the resumed stream and the resumed model state are not aligned.

Goals:
- Implement a lightweight server-side "sequence-gap detector" to detect missing sequence numbers on reconnects and surface clear diagnostics.
- Add a short-lived replay/backfill buffer and a deterministic backfill protocol so clients can resume without re-generating from scratch or receiving duplicate tokens.
- Expose resume metadata and checksums in the SSE event envelope (sequence_num, resume_token, shard_checksum) and update SDKs to use them.
- Provide fallbacks (graceful degrade to polled completion) when backfill isn't possible (e.g., buffer expired or cross-shard resume).

Technical design (high level):
1) Event envelope changes: every SSE event includes sequence_num (monotonic per-request), resume_token (opaque server token), and short checksum of the last KV-frame. This remains backwards compatible: older SDKs ignore extra fields.
2) Server-side replay buffer: keep a ring buffer of the last N events per active request (configurable, default 30s or 2k tokens). On reconnect with a resume_token, the gateway attempts to validate the resume against the checksum and sequence window.
3) Sequence-gap detector: when a client reconnects with last_event_id, compare sequence_num continuity. If gap detected, attempt to emit a backfill patch of missing events. If unable to backfill, return a single SSE control event (resume_required) with code and human readable reason to trigger client fallback.
4) Cross-shard and eviction policy: Dedicated/Private deployments may route to different workers. If the resume_token maps to a worker that no longer holds the buffer, gateway checks the last known checkpoint and either (a) proxy to the original worker if still available, (b) attempt a reconstructed backfill from model KV checkpoints up to a safety limit, or (c) return resume_required.
5) SDK changes: Add automatic resume on reconnect using last_event_id + resume_token, validate incoming checksum, apply backfill patches idempotently, and expose a clear error if resume_required occurs.

Reproduction steps (internal):
- Run load test that injects short TCP resets from a synthetic LB after 150-400ms of streaming.
- Use streaming test prompt that generates many small tokens (e.g., tokenizer creates many sub-tokens) to amplify sequence boundaries.
- Observe server logs for sequence_num discontinuities and confirm duplicate or missing tokens.

Observations from incidents:
- Customer REDACTED-1 (hosted): observed ~3% of streamed sessions with missing trailing tokens after reconnect; support ticket 2026-03-02-RED-81.
- Customer REDACTED-2 (dedicated): duplicates when autoscaler moved worker mid-stream; autoscaler events correlate with missing replay buffer entries.
- Private deployment (on-prem): operator reported buffer eviction during node restart; restart window longer than buffer TTL caused resume_required response.

Proposed implementation plan and milestones:
- Spike (2d): prototype sequence_num envelope and small ring buffer in gateway runtime; add simple resume control event. (owner: Michael Chen)
- Design review (1d): share design doc and compatibility matrix with SDK and Console teams. (owner: Asha Patel)
- Implementation (5d): implement detector + buffer + backfill handlers in runtime; add config flags (buffer_size, ttl, cross_shard_retry). Include metrics (resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_fail_reasons). (owner: Michael Chen)
- SDK updates (3d parallel): add resume handshake logic and idempotent patch application in JS and Python SDKs. (owner: SDK team)
- Integration tests (2d): add chaos tests with LB resets, worker handoff, and replay failure cases. (owner: QA)
- Canary rollout (2d): enable feature behind runtime flag; start on staging, then small subset of production customers including non-critical tenants; monitor metrics and SLOs. (owner: Infra/Oncall)
- Full rollout + docs (2d): update API docs, migration notes, and support runbook.

Rollout considerations and safety:
- Feature gated via config per-customer to allow quick disable. Default disabled for Private on-prem installs (operators opt-in).
- Telemetry: track resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, duplicate_token_rate, average_replay_latency. Create alerts on >1% resume_failure for high-traffic tenants.
- Backwards compatibility: older SDKs will still receive sequence fields but ignore them; gateway must never change event boundaries for legacy clients.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for sequence arithmetic, checksum validation, and ring buffer eviction.
- End-to-end tests simulating reconnects with deterministic RNG to assert no missing/duplicate tokens in resumed flows.
- Load tests to measure CPU/latency cost of maintaining per-request ring buffers at 10k concurrent streams; add autoscaling safeguards.

Telemetry + Observability updates:
- Add tracing span on resume path (resume_attempt, resume_backfill_hit/miss, resume_reconstructed).
- Console dashboard: per-tenant resume success rate, top resume_fail_reasons, and per-model token re-gen cost estimate.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Buffer size vs. memory footprint: conservative defaults, allow per-tenant tuning for Dedicated.
- Cross-shard reconstruction cost vs. user experience: how far back to reconstruct before returning resume_required? (default: 2k tokens / 30s)
- Whether to persist minimal checkpoints to fast storage (ramdisk/ephemeral SSD) for longer resume windows; increases complexity for Private installs.

Done criteria:
- New SSE envelope fields in runtime and SDK (JS/Python) implemented and backwards compatible.
- Resume detector and backfill buffer present with feature flags; can resume successfully for >99% reconnects in staged chaos tests.
- Playbook/Runbook updated and support team trained.
- No regression on streaming latency p50/p95 beyond 5% in production canary.

comments: 2026-03-05 - Asha: Created ticket after support escalations from two customers. Filed initial design doc and requested a spike. @Michael assigned.
2026-03-06 - Michael: Completed spike. Confirmed ring buffer prototype can backfill up to 2k tokens with ~0.5ms median cost. Pushed PR to runtime (draft).
2026-03-08 - Design review: feedback from SDK team to expose resume_token as opaque string, not JSON, to avoid parsing mismatch. Updated design doc.
2026-03-09 - QA: Added chaos scenarios for worker handoff. Observed resume_success_rate drop to 78% when buffer TTL=10s; raising default TTL to 30s improved success to 98%.

2026-03-10 - Michael: Implemented metrics (resume_attempts/resume_success). Creating canary plan and runbook for support. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4291 (ready for review).
